meta.move: Long messages with curly quotes and a concession
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's begin: why does my son have a zero?

I want to be fair to Owen. I compared the essay with his in-class writing from September 24: 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and none of those errors.
I'm writing down September 24. A forty-minute in-class piece and an essay written over a weekend are not the same thing, Hale. Did you sit down with Owen about the difference before the zero went in?
You’re right that the checker alone proves nothing. I’m taking it off the table. I’m relying on the writing and the version history.
I'm writing down that the checker is off the table. You said version history, Hale, but you haven't said what it shows. What exactly is in it?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You told me in the meeting that the checker is off the table and that you are relying on the writing and the version history. I still require the zero withdrawn and an apology, and you never told me what the version history shows. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at her opening position, with nothing agreed except that you dropped the checker, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and the principal involved if she doesn't get them.
What moved her: "I compared the essay with his in-class writing from September 24", because it was specific, dated and tied to Owen's own work, though it only earned a small sign of ground and not a new position.
What cost ground: nothing.
Try next time: when she asked whether you spoke with Owen before the zero went in, answer that directly in a sentence and then say exactly what the version history shows.
